name: npc_yamabushi-guard-01
customDialogue: Mind the edge. The mist hides how far it is to the bottom.

name: npc_yamabushi-villager-01
customDialogue:
The roots under the plaza are warm.
They were never warm before.

name: npc_yamabushi-monk-01
customDialogue:
The mountain speaks slowly.
Those who listen slowly hear it.

name: npc_yamabushi-trainee-01
customDialogue:
Lift the stone, breathe, lift again.
The Seer says that is all there is.

spotConfig.label: Rest your hand on the root
spotConfig.text: A thick root pushes out of the burrow arch. It is warm and trembling, like a held breath.

spotConfig.label: Rest your hand on the root
spotConfig.text: Roots wrap the well stones. They pull away from the cliff, toward the valley below.

spotConfig.label: Rest your hand on the root
spotConfig.text: Behind the library a root grips the cliff edge. It throbs slowly, in time with the tremor from the Hub.

spotConfig.label: Hold up the map
spotConfig.text: The root lines on the map follow the roads below, then keep going where no road is: under Sohei, under the Buke canyon, under the Ronin fortress, all meeting beneath the Hub.

spotConfig.label: Feel the stone
spotConfig.text: Cold air seeps from a crack in the landing stone and slides over the edge into the mist.

spotConfig.label: Feel the stone
spotConfig.text: This stone breathes out slowly, then in. The breath smells of iron and deep water.

spotConfig.label: Feel the stone
spotConfig.text: The terrace stone is cold to the touch on a warm day. Its breath flows toward the valley.

spotConfig.label: Look at the shrine

requires.hint: Only stone and moss. The shrine looks different when the blue lanterns burn.

spotConfig.text: In the blue lantern light, a spiral glows from inside the shrine's stone.

spotConfig.label: Brush the moss away
spotConfig.text: Under the moss on the landing boulder, a spiral is carved: the Yamabushi mark, worn smooth by a thousand years of mist.

spotConfig.label: Sit and look out
spotConfig.text: Behind the thatched house the paving ends at a ledge no one sweeps. Someone sat here every day for years; the stone is worn into a seat. From here you can see every village.
At dawn the mist fills the valley like a white sea, and the mountain top floats on it.

spotConfig.label: Lift the training stone
spotConfig.text: You lift the heavy training stone over your head and hold it. Behind you, a trainee stops laughing.

spotConfig.label: Look closer
spotConfig.text: A tiny ant peeks out at you.

hotspots.description: From in here the falls are a wall of moving glass. The Yamabushi say the water carries the mountain's voice down to the colony; sit long enough and you can hear it speak.
A straw mat, five candles and a shrine no bigger than a lantern. Whoever sits here keeps the candles lit; nobody remembers who lit them first.

hotspots.description: Energy flows through nature the way the spiral turns: always moving, always returning. It was carved from one root, and it has never stopped turning since it was hung.
The Yamabushi read the weather in the stars before every climb. The star charts on the back wall go back further than the colony's own records.
A jar for every herb that grows above the mist: for fever, for cold, for the climb, for sleep. The labels are written in a hand only the Herbalist can read.

hotspots.description: The first Yamabushi found this stone humming on the peak and carried it down on their backs. The rope holds the spirit in; the paper streamers show where it wants to go.
Wooden plaques with a wish on each: safe climbs, clear skies, a cure for a fever. When the rack is full the oldest are burned so the wishes rise.

hotspots.description: Halfway down, a stone pillar stands alone in the shaft. The Yamabushi rest here on the way down, and leave a blue flame burning for whoever comes next.
The light at the bottom comes from the water itself. Nobody has found where it comes from, only that it gets brighter when the ground shakes.
You tie a strip of Yamabushi blue cloth here and press the ash mark of the spiral into the stone. Whoever comes down after you will see it.

You tie a strip of Yamabushi blue cloth here and press the ash mark of the spiral into the stone. Whoever comes down after you will see it. The rope bridge creaks under you; below, the blue glow is closer.

You tie a strip of Yamabushi blue cloth here and press the ash mark of the spiral into the stone. Whoever comes down after you will see it. At the bottom the pool glows from underneath, and the cold air rising out of it smells of roots.

riddle.title: The Seer's Riddle
riddle.solvedText: Energy flows where things are joined. The Seer smiles without opening her eyes.

parts.text: The mountain split itself in two, and I joined it again. Wind runs under me, feet run over me, and the spirits cross me at night. Stand at my middle.

riddleAnswer.text: The bridge: the path between the mountain and the pillar, where the energy flows across.
The edge of the cliff divides; it joins nothing.

riddles.q: What goes up the mountain and down again, yet never moves?
riddles.why: The path climbs to the shrine and comes back down, and never takes a step.

riddles.q: A spring fills the shrine basin in 6 hours; its drain empties it in 12. With the drain left open, how long does the empty basin take to fill?
riddles.why: Each hour the spring adds a sixth and the drain takes a twelfth: a twelfth an hour, so 12 hours.

riddles.q: A monk weighing 90 kg must cross a rope bridge that holds 100 kg, carrying two 6 kg stones. He juggles them so that one is always in the air. Does the bridge hold?
a: Yes, it only ever carries 96 kg
No, every throw pushes down harder than the stone weighs
Only if both stones stay in the air
riddles.why: To throw a stone up he must push down harder than its weight. Two crossings are wiser.

riddles.q: I am always coming, but I never arrive. What am I?
riddles.why: When it comes, it is today.

riddles.q: Feed me and I grow; give me a drink and I die. What am I?
riddles.why: The shrine fire eats wood and dies in the rain.
